html:
In 1804 the Japanese surgeon Hanaoka Seishū removed a breast cancer from a woman under general anaesthesia. It is the earliest well-recorded operation of its kind, more than forty years before ether was first used in the United States.

Hanaoka worked in Kii province, near today's Wakayama. He knew Chinese herbal medicine and also Western surgery learned through Dutch books, the field of Dutch learning opened by works like the Kaitai Shinsho.

He spent years making a herbal drink, tsūsensan, based on plants including datura, a nightshade. It put patients into a deep sleep for hours. He is said to have tested it on his mother and his wife, who lost her sight as a result.

His 1804 patient was a 60-year-old woman. Hanaoka went on to operate on many more patients and trained many students. Because Japan was cut off from most of the world under Tokugawa rule, his work stayed unknown in the West for a long time.
